entries.name: Polar bear
entries.migrates: follows the sea ice edge with the seasons
behaviour: hunts seals at breathing holes and on the ice
solitary except mothers and cubs
mothers den in snow banks for the winter
entries.notes: The Arctic's apex predator; the whole ice food web (seals, krill) exists to feed it. gestation_days includes delayed implantation.

entries.name: Walrus
entries.migrates: seasonal ice-edge movements and haul-outs
behaviour: sucks clams from the seabed with its tongue like a piston
hauls out in enormous noisy aggregations on ice and rock
both sexes carry tusks; males fight for harem-like positions
entries.notes: The moustache first: 400-700 vibrissae. gestation_days is about 15-16 months including delayed implantation, the longest of the pinnipeds.

entries.name: Killer whale
behaviour: lives in matrilineal pods with pod-specific dialects
hunts cooperatively; some pods specialise in fish, others in marine mammals
echolocates and coordinates attacks

voxel_model.pattern: white eye patches and white underside

entries.notes: Different ecotypes prey on different things; a fish-eater and a seal-eater are nearly different animals in practice. gestation_days ~15-18 months, exact value varies by ecotype.

entries.name: Bowhead whale
entries.migrates: follows the spring ice retreat north and the autumn freeze south
behaviour: breaks new ice with its reinforced skull
sings long, distinctive songs; 184 distinct songs recorded in one population
slow, huge, solitary or in small pods; eats ~1.8 tonnes a day
entries.notes: Enormous arched skull and longest baleen of any whale. Likely the longest-lived mammal, over 200 years; an adult carries a 17th-century bomb lance in one documented case. gestation_days 13-14 months.

entries.name: Humpback whale
entries.migrates: polar feeding grounds in summer, tropical breeding grounds in winter
behaviour: famous bubble-net feeding: rings of bubbles trap schools of fish
leaping and pectoral-fin slapping displays
males sing complex songs in breeding grounds

voxel_model.pattern: white throat grooves and unique fluke pattern

entries.notes: Visits both poles seasonally; the bubble-net hunt is the single best set-piece a frozen ocean can host. gestation_days ~11-11.5 months.

entries.name: Common minke whale
entries.migrates: seasonal; poleward in summer to feed, equatorward in winter
behaviour: curiosity approaches boats
fast, lunge-feeding on small schools
often travels singly or in pairs
entries.notes: The smallest rorqual and the most numerous large whale; the Antarctic minke (B. bonaerensis) is the southern twin. gestation_days ~10-11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Emperor penguin
behaviour: only bird to breed through the polar winter on bare ice
father incubates the single egg on his feet all winter while mother feeds at sea
endures -50 C and 200 km/h katabatic winds huddled in groups

voxel_model.pattern: yellow ear patches and pale breast

entries.notes: The siege: no food for four months while the chick hatches. gestation_days is egg incubation on the feet. Dives deeper than any bird, over 500 m.

entries.name: Adélie penguin
behaviour: builds nests of pebbles on rocky ice-free coasts
massive colonies; very noisy and sociable
'tambourine dance' displays and fights over pebbles
entries.notes: The penguin most people picture; the vast pebble-nest colonies on bare rock are the Antarctic's biggest spectacle. gestation_days is egg incubation.

entries.name: Chinstrap penguin
behaviour: pebble-nests and scrapes on open beaches
lies flat and rocks its head before fleeing
famously quarrelsome over nesting sites
entries.notes: Named for the black strap under its chin; one Deception Island colony held millions of birds, though chinstrap numbers are falling as krill declines.

entries.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
behaviour: hops up steep rocks with both feet together
yellow plume eyebrows and a red bill
lays two eggs, usually raising only the second
entries.notes: The punk-rock penguin; nests on storm-beaten rocky coasts, not ice. gestation_days (incubation) is roughly five weeks but varies by subspecies.

entries.name: Ringed seal
entries.migrates: follows the ice edge in the Bering Sea and Okhotsk Sea
behaviour: maintains breathing holes through ice up to 1.8 m thick with its claws
digs snow lairs over breathing holes to pup
solitary; separates itself from other seals by hundreds of metres
entries.notes: The polar bear's staple; it survives where no other seal can, under thick multi-year ice. Gestation ~9 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Bearded seal
entries.migrates: moves with the southern ice edge
behaviour: feeds by suction on bottom-dwelling invertebrates, like a walrus
long sweeping whiskers and vibrissae-plumed muzzle
males trill underwater in complex songs to attract females
entries.notes: Second largest seal in the Arctic and a key subsistence species. gestation_days ~11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Harp seal
entries.migrates: long-distance seasonal migrations between feeding and whelping ice
behaviour: gathers in huge whelping congregations on moving pack ice
newborn pups are white 'whitecoats' nursing ~12 days
famous as the regulated Canadian seal hunt
entries.notes: The 'saddleback'; males carry a dark harp-shaped patch on their backs. gestation_days ~11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Hooded seal
entries.migrates: follows the pack ice through the North Atlantic
behaviour: male inflates a nasal hood and a red throat sac as display over the ice
pups are weaned after only ~4 days, the shortest lactation of any mammal
deep divers; crashes through ice when startled
entries.notes: Sprays the red throat sac like a bloodied balloon in display; 4-day weaning means the mother does not eat ashore. gestation_days ~11.5 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Ribbon seal
entries.migrates: follows the Bering Sea ice south in winter and north in summer

breeding.season: spring (pups born on drifting pack ice)

behaviour: striking dark coat with white ribbon bands and a white face mask
nests alone on moving pack ice rather than fast ice
supple and agile for a seal; rarely hauls out in groups
entries.notes: The Bering Sea's harlequin seal, a northern Pacific endemic; a strong reason a cold world needs both polar oceans to feel different.

entries.name: Antarctic fur seal
entries.migrates: seasonal between colonies and foraging grounds
behaviour: breeds in enormous colonies, mostly on subantarctic islands like South Georgia
males guard harems and fight fiercely on beaches
stunning recovery from near-extinction by 1900
entries.notes: An eared seal, not a true seal; dense waterproof underfur made it the target of 19th-century sealing. gestation_days ~9 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Weddell seal
behaviour: maintains breathing holes through metres of fast ice all winter, like a ringed seal
deepest-diving seal; past 600 m for over an hour
grooms the ice edge with its claws to keep holes open
entries.notes: The only mammal living year-round on Antarctic fast ice; its songs under the ice are the Antarctic's hidden soundtrack. gestation_days ~10-11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Crabeater seal
entries.migrates: follows the pack ice as it advances and retreats
behaviour: sieve-like interlocking lobed molars strain krill from the water
most abundant pinniped on Earth, an estimated 10-15 million adults
solitary but congregates in loose associations near ice floes
entries.notes: Despite the name it eats almost nothing but krill; likely the most numerous seal on the planet. gestation_days ~11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Leopard seal
behaviour: hunts penguins by ambush at the water's edge, shaking them like a dog
takes warm-blooded prey other Antarctic predators ignore
males sing for hours daily underwater in the spring
entries.notes: The true apex of the Antarctic sea; kills penguins by flailing them against the water's surface. One human fatality recorded (Kirsty Brown, 2003).

entries.name: Ross seal
entries.migrates: follows the pack ice edge
behaviour: lays its upper body flat and lifts its head like a cobra when alarmed
deeply divergent skull; enormous eyes adapted to darkness
least-known of the four Antarctic pack-ice seals; rarely approached
entries.notes: The mystery seal: enormous deep-set eyes and a raised-cobra posture. Almost nothing is known of its breeding — honest nulls here.

entries.name: Southern elephant seal
entries.migrates: huge migrations between breeding beaches and deep foraging grounds
behaviour: largest pinniped; bulls grow a proboscis nose and rear up to fight for harems
fasts completely for the 3-month breeding and moulting season
dives ~1.5 km deep and stays down for 2 hours, longer than any tollerant mammal air breather
entries.notes: Bulls hold harems of 20-50 females and starve while they fight. gestation_days ~11 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Narwhal
entries.migrates: summers in high-Arctic fjords and inlets, winters at the ice edge
behaviour: males grow a spiralled ivory tusk up to 3 m (a modified upper canine)
travels in pods of tens to thousands; crowds into ice cracks in winter
heavily echolocating deep diver
entries.notes: The unicorn whale; nobody knows quite why males carry the tusk, though 'tusking' jousts suggest competition and display. gestation ~14 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Beluga whale
entries.migrates: summers in warm shallow estuaries and river mouths, winters at the ice edge
behaviour: pure white, with no dorsal fin and a melon forehead it reshapes to focus sound
molts to pure white once a year; grey as a calf
highly vocal; follows convoy and boats; calls non-stop between pod members
entries.notes: The 'sea canary' — so chatty it may shadow fishing boats out of curiosity. gestation_days ~13-14 months including delayed implantation.

entries.name: Atlantic puffin
entries.migrates: spends winters alone on the open North Atlantic
behaviour: nests in burrows in cliff-top grass
carries dozens of fish crosswise in its bill to the burrow
orange triangular bill glows in the breeding season
entries.notes: Nests in hand-burrows in cliff grass; the winter harvest of Norway, Iceland and the Faroes. gestation_days is egg incubation (~6 weeks).

entries.name: Arctic tern
entries.migrates: Arctic to Antarctic and back each year — the longest known migration, up to ~70,000 km annually
behaviour: chases surface fish with angled dives
aggressively mobs anyone near its nest, including humans
two annual summers, one per pole; lives up to 30+ years
entries.notes: The longest commuter alive; a bird banding study showed one bird that saw both poles every year for decades. gestation_days is egg incubation (~3-4 weeks).

entries.name: Thick-billed murre (Brünnich's guillemot)
behaviour: stands shoulder-to-shoulder on sheer cliff ledges, holding one teardrop-shaped egg on its feet
the chick jumps from the cliff to the sea at 2-3 weeks, guided to the water by the male
one of the most numerous seabirds in the Arctic
entries.notes: Cliff-bound like a tiny razorbill; the chick's jump is a founding image for any arctic cliff scene. gestation_days is egg incubation (~4-5 weeks).

entries.name: Common eider
entries.migrates: short coastal migrations; large winter flocks on ice-free coasts
behaviour: famous for its insulating down, harvested sustainably for centuries in Iceland (eiderdown)
dives in coastal shallows for shellfish
drakes are black-and-white with a green nape; hens are mottled brown
entries.notes: The down of eider nests is gathered, not plucked — an honest, renewable harvest. gestation_days is egg incubation of roughly four weeks.

entries.name: Northern fulmar
entries.migrates: moves with the ice edge and fishing grounds
behaviour: glides for hours on stiff wings low over cold seas
defends itself with a foul vomited stomach oil
follows ships for offal; abundant at polar fishing grounds
entries.notes: A tube-nose relative of albatrosses; its projectile vomit is the famous defence at every polar colony. gestation_days is egg incubation of roughly six weeks.

entries.name: Ivory gull
entries.migrates: follows the Arctic pack ice
behaviour: immaculate all-white gull of the high Arctic pack ice
shadows polar bears to pick over seal remains
small, scattered colonies on remote ice-free cliffs
entries.notes: Near-threatened and declining with the ice; the pure-white ghost haunting bear kills. A rare spawn should feel like an event.

entries.name: Snow petrel
behaviour: small pure-white tube-nose with dark eyes; nests in rocky crevices and scree
flies on short, bowed wings close to the ice
called the 'ice dove' for its appearance against blue ice
entries.notes: An albatross-relative that breeds on bare Antarctic rock; a clean white speck against ice waves — rare and beautiful.

entries.name: Arctic cod (polar cod)
entries.migrates: schools move with the shifting under-ice zones
behaviour: feeds among the ice crystals themselves, including on ice algae
keystone food link: everything in the Arctic eats it
glycol-rich blood lets it swim in near-freezing brine channels
entries.notes: The calorie backbone of the Arctic; lose the ice algae and the cod, and the ringed seals and polar bears follow.

entries.name: Greenland shark
entries.migrates: seasonal depth movements rather than long migrations
behaviour: grows ~1 cm a year; may take 150 years to reach maturity
loiters near seal sleeping orcas and fishing boats
sees almost nothing — much of its cornea hosts a parasitic copepod
its raw flesh is poisonous from trimethylamine oxide
entries.notes: The longest-lived vertebrate known (272+ years, possibly 400-500) and the slowest fish; eats carrion and sleeping seals. gestation is estimated at 8-18 years.

entries.name: Arctic char
entries.migrates: anadromous; spawning runs up rivers in autumn
behaviour: the world's northernmost freshwater fish; a salmon-relative with spectacular spawning colours
runs from the frozen sea into Arctic rivers to spawn
tough, and even landlocked clear lakes hold char

voxel_model.pattern: red belly, pale-spotted flanks in spawning males

entries.notes: The salmon of the Arctic Ocean: a landward chapter of the frozen ocean. When the runs are on, fjords boil with char and bears.

entries.name: Antarctic toothfish (Antarctic sea bass)
entries.migrates: deep vertical and ontogenetic migration
behaviour: large deep-sea predator beneath the ice shelf, the target of the controversial 'Chilean sea bass' fishery
cold as stone and slow-growing; lives decades
prey of sperm whales and elephant seals, its signature predators
entries.notes: Signature prey item of Antarctic megafauna; the longline that chases it defines a whole deep-ocean economy. Grows past 2 m.

entries.name: Mackerel icefish
behaviour: unique among vertebrates: most of the family lacks haemoglobin, so the blood runs clear
antifreeze glycoproteins stop the blood freezing in ice-cold water
schools over continental shelves; key prey for penguins and seals
entries.notes: The only vertebrate with clear blood; an extinction-tech tree waiting for a game that asks 'what would fish look like if they evolved under ice?'

entries.name: Antarctic krill
entries.migrates: follows the sea ice edge in vast swarms
behaviour: swarms can number in the millions of tonnes over hundreds of km^2
grazes phytoplankton and scrapes algae from the underside of the ice
four or five years between hatch and first breeding; keys to the whole Antarctic food web
entries.notes: The single most important species in the Southern Ocean; every baleen, seal and penguin in this file eats krill.

entries.name: Colossal squid
entries.migrates: ontogenetic; young live shallow, adults dive 1-2 km down
behaviour: the largest invertebrate known, heavier than the giant squid at equal length
amber-eyed, hooked tentacles, and very large for a squid
preyed on almost exclusively by sperm whales, which bear its scars
entries.notes: The deep-sea boss of the Southern Ocean; known mostly from beaks in sperm whale stomachs and trawl finds. Almost no field observations exist.
